mcat_description.short: Prefabricated Buildings are factory-engineered structures — primarily Pre-Engineered Buildings (PEB) in steel — where all structural components are designed, fabricated off-site, and assembled on location, covering industrial sheds, warehouses, commercial buildings, and residential structures.
mcat_description.long: Prefabricated Buildings in the Indian market encompass structures where primary components — steel frames, roof and wall cladding panels, purlins, columns, and secondary members — are manufactured in a controlled factory environment and bolted or welded together on-site, dramatically reducing construction time versus conventional RCC methods. The dominant commercial form is the Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) in structural steel, used for warehouses, factories, logistics parks, cold storage, and commercial showrooms, with steel structure accounting for over 52% of market share. A growing secondary segment includes Light Gauge Steel Frame (LGSF) residential homes, panel-based modular buildings, and precast concrete structures serving housing, institutional, and government projects. Structural design must comply with the National Building Code of India 2016 (NBC 2016) and relevant BIS standards including IS 15916 for prefabricated concrete and IS 11447 for precast elements, with seismic zone compliance mandatory across all types.

market_context: The Indian prefabricated buildings market is dominated by Pre-Engineered Buildings (PEB) in structural steel, with steel structure accounting for over 52% of product share and the industrial sector (warehouses, factories, logistics) commanding nearly 49% of end-user demand. The market reached USD 2.26 Billion in 2025 and is projected to grow at 12.38% CAGR through 2034, driven by PLI scheme factory construction, e-commerce warehouse expansion, and cold chain infrastructure. Key Indian PEB manufacturers include Interarch, EPACK Prefab, Pennar Industries, Kirby Building Systems, Everest Industries, and Zamil Steel. A growing secondary segment — LGSF (Light Gauge Steel Frame) residential homes and modular/panel-based buildings — is gaining traction under PMAY government housing schemes and private residential demand. Structural compliance is governed by NBC 2016 (BIS), with IS 15916 (prefabricated concrete), IS 11447 (precast elements), and IS 1343 (prestressed concrete) as the key BIS standards; seismic zone compliance is mandatory. Buyers evaluate PEB suppliers on clear-span capability, steel grade, erection timeline, wind and seismic zone design, and ISO 9001 certification. The term 'PEB' is the dominant trade vocabulary in the Indian B2B market; 'prefab building' and 'readymade ghar' are used in residential/smaller-scale contexts.
